Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Asset Management Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, during the Q&A session, please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Asset Management's Q4 results. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Reed, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Investment Officer; and David Wong, Head of Distribution.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Reed.

Johnathan Reed: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q4 2023. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust net inflows, market appreciation, and our multi-channel distribution momentum. Our AUM grew to $525 billion.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Johnathan. From a financial perspective, Apex Asset Management delivered strong results in Q4 2023. Our revenue was $2.41 billion, representing an 11% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by AUM expansion and resilient fee rates. Our expenses were $1.05 billion, resulting in net income of $850 million. We continue to manage our expenses prudently, as evidenced by our improving efficiency ratios.

Let me provide some color on the critical linkage between our assets under management and revenue generation, which remains the cornerstone of our business model. Approximately 92% of our total revenue stems from management fees, predominantly calculated as a percentage of average daily AUM at our blended fee rate across equities, fixed income, alternatives, and multi-asset solutions. Our average management fee rate for the quarter held steady at 48 basis points, down just 2 basis points year-over-year due to modest fee compression in our passive ETF suite, but partially offset by higher-margin active strategies in private credit and infrastructure. This stability underscores our disciplined pricing framework amid industry-wide pressures from low-cost providers like Vanguard and BlackRock's iShares platform.

We ended the quarter with $525 billion in AUM, up 8% sequentially and 12% year-over-year. This growth stemmed from market performance contributing about $22 billion, or 4.5% quarter-over-quarter—our equity AUM at 55% of total benefited from the S&P 500's rally, adding $14 billion, while fixed income saw $3 billion and alternatives $5 billion from drawdowns. Net flows were a standout at $12 billion positive, the strongest since late 2022, lifting revenue by an incremental $57 million annualized at our blended fee rate—institutional channels delivered $9 billion, led by ESG-enhanced active equity from sovereign wealth funds and Nordic pensions, while retail added $3 billion via low-cost UCITS ETFs. FX impacts added $5 billion from euro strengthening. Average AUM of $512 billion, up 9%, multiplied by our 48 bps rate, yielded a $110 million mechanical lift from expansion alone, with performance fees adding $85 million, up 25% from PE realizations.

Regionally, North America at 62% of AUM contributed robustly, EMEA grew to 22% on MiFID II tailwinds, and APAC at 12% accelerated with China A-shares. We're mitigating AUM volatility through product innovation like three new active ETFs garnering $1.2 billion seed, scale efficiencies dropping our fee-related expense ratio to 22%, and client diversification with 2.4% organic net flow margins.

Turning to efficiency metrics, which are a cornerstone of our competitive edge, our weighted-average expense ratio for the quarter came in at 42 basis points, a 10 bps improvement year-over-year and better than recent quarters. This marks 12 straight quarters of decline, driven by AUM scale to $525 billion—up 18% on $45 billion organic inflows—and cost discipline. Trailing 12-month basis, it's 43 bps, below the industry average of 52 bps and peers like State Street at 47 bps.

By product: ETFs and index at 52% of AUM hold 12 bps, with our core S&P 500 ETF at 7 bps undercutting Vanguard while flows hit $28 billion; active equities at 28% improved to 62 bps via quant overlays reducing research costs; fixed income and alternatives at 20% dropped to 38 bps leveraging blockchain for custody savings. Regionally, US at 38 bps benefits from ETF growth, Europe at 48 bps clawed back via feeders, APAC/EM at 55 bps trending down post-partnerships.

Drivers include scale diluting fixed costs by 22% as expenses rose just 8% to levels supporting $2.8 million revenue per employee, top quartile per benchmarks. Technical initiatives like our cloud-native ops on AWS automating 65% middle-office, AI cutting trading costs 14 bps, gen-AI client bots targeting 20% call center savings, and tokenization processing $10 billion settlements. We're building moats with smart beta hybrids at 25 bps, guiding full-year 41 bps expense ratio, aiming sub-40 bps by 2025 on $300 billion ETF flows.

Now, on net flows by channel, which totaled a robust $18.2 billion for the quarter—our strongest in years, up 45% year-over-year against a volatile macro. Ending AUM hit levels supporting 125 bps organic growth.

Institutional channel led with +$11.4 billion, 63% of total, outpacing peers—$8.2 billion into fixed income like Core Plus Bond and LDI as pensions repositioned, $2.1 billion ESG credit. North America $6.3 billion, EMEA $3.1 billion gilts, APAC $1.5 billion Samurai ETF. YoY up 62%, low 0.8% redemptions via Aladdin analytics retaining 92%.

Retail +$4.8 billion, 26%, best since ETF boom—$3.1 billion ETFs like S&P 500 ESG capturing share, $1.2 billion SMAs tax alpha. US $3.4 billion via robo integrations onboarding 45,000 clients, Europe $0.9 billion UCITS, APAC $0.5 billion. Rotation from cash, 18% digital conversion.

Alternatives +$2.0 billion, 11%, up 35% YoY—$1.1 billion private credit 9.2% yield, $0.6 billion real assets data centers. 70% institutional, EMEA hotspot $0.8 billion AIFMD, US $0.9 billion insurance. Tailwinds: $500 million GP stakes seed, blockchain NAV cutting lags 40%.

Forward, $20-25 billion annualized flows on Fed cuts, new alts ETFs, APAC hub $10 billion pipeline, GenAI forecasting sub-1% churn, quant tuck-in. This validates our hybrid strategy, 4.2% organic YTD vs. industry 2.8%.

Before handing back, a detailed update on our capital allocation strategy, a cornerstone of delivering shareholder value with over $525 billion AUM up 12% on strong flows. Philosophy: consistent shareholder returns, high-ROI platform investments, opportunistic M&A. Deployed $2.8 billion FCF at 22% margin on revenue base, zero net debt, AAA balance sheet.

Shareholder returns aggressive: Q4 $450 million buybacks at $128/share retiring 1.8% float, YTD $1.4 billion; 12% dividend hike to $0.65/share, 17th year growth, 4.2% total yield premium to peers. $2 billion window for dips at 12.5x forward FEE.

Reinvesting 25-30% FCF, $700-850 million: $250 million ApexOne Phase II live on 65% equity AUM, cutting costs 15%, boosting smart-beta ETF $18 billion flows. EMEA $75 million distribution reversing outflows $5.2 billion new ETF; APAC $120 million alternatives $10 billion credit fund 1.2% fee.

Trends: passive/ETFs 42% AUM 28 bps holding vs. Vanguard, alts 18% $95 billion growing 22% on $28 billion flows pensions rotating.

M&A: two tuck-ins YTD $830 million adding $45 billion AUM 10x multiple 15% EPS accretive; $1.5 billion dry powder 8-12x for digital assets, RIA aggregators 1-2 H1 2024.

FY24 guidance: 50-55% buybacks/dividends $1.8-2.0 billion, 25-30% capex $900 million-$1.1 billion, 15-20% M&A $500-700 million, balance cash. 12-15% FEE CAGR vs. industry 8%, 45% payout. Battle-tested 18% TSR beating index.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities and alternatives. We are navigating the current market environment by emphasizing active alpha in niches like private credit and ESG-enhanced products, while maintaining a 70/30 active/passive mix. We launched the Apex S&P 500 ESG Enhanced ETF this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $12 billion AUM and 35% YoY flows amid sustainable demand.

David Wong: Thank you, Lisa. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF and SMA funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in key regions are paying off. As we wrap up a transformative quarter, our distribution partnerships and channel expansion continue as a cornerstone of organic growth. With $525 billion AUM up 12% year-over-year, we posted record $28 billion Q4 net inflows, full-year $112 billion up 25% vs. industry 8% per Morningstar. Over 60% or $68 billion from expanded channels.

Core partnerships shone: Charles Schwab alliance year three onboarded 450 RIAs via marketplace, $15 billion NNA into low-cost ETFs/SMAs, 2.5% share gain YoY at 28 bps fees; Apex S&P 500 ESG ETF $12 billion 35% flows. Fidelity deepened with 15 new models like Core Bond Ladder SMA, $9 billion institutional YTD, 40% adoption via APIs, 18% QoQ performance fees.

Beyond wirehouses 15% top-10 share, digital wins: Wealthfront white-label direct indexing $4.2 billion HNW tax-alpha 20-30 bps outperformance, 85% retention. ETF shelf-space: Global Tech Innovators APTX $8 billion, 50% flows Robinhood/SoFi 40% millennial $6 billion YTD 300% ramp thematic shift.

U.S. 82% AUM robust, Europe UCITS €5 billion Q4 Eurozone Equity top-quartile 12% returns 45 bps; Nordics Nordnet 1.2% share MiFID II. APAC 22% YoY to $45 billion: DBS JV $3.8 billion small-cap, China QDII $1.2 billion onshore tapping 15% CAGR, EM India/Brazil $2.1 billion 18% IRRs.

Infrastructure: ApexFlow on Snowflake/Aladdin cuts time-to-market 60%, APIs 200+ partners Reg BI/PRIIPs, direct indexing 50,000 underlyings 1.2 million trades/month 99.9% uptime.

Fee stability: active alpha alts/multi-asset 52 bps up 5 bps, ML partner selection >10% RIA growth Envestnet doubling to 28 sleeves, 45% ESG flows $40 trillion trend.

Forward: $130-150 billion 2024 flows 40% new channels, TradePMR RIA $20 billion SMA, Plaid neobanks retirement. Mitigate volatility 70/30 mix <2% churn.

Our engine blends scale, tech, partnerships for resilient growth.

Johnathan Reed: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes our disciplined capital allocation, product innovation, and channel diversification to drive fee-related earnings growth at 12-15% CAGR through 2026.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. As a reminder, please limit to one question and one follow-up. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Morningstar.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the net flows by channel and how they tie into your distribution expansion?

Michael Chen: Good morning, Emily. Absolutely, our $18.2 billion Q2-equivalent flows were diversified: institutional $11.4 billion led by fixed income and ESG, retail $4.8 billion on ETFs and SMAs with strong digital uptake, alternatives $2.0 billion private credit and real assets. This ties directly to partnerships like Schwab and Fidelity driving 60% of full-year $112 billion, outpacing industry via tech-enabled channels and regional pushes in EMEA/APAC.

Emily Carter: Thank you. And a follow-up on how AUM changes specifically impacted revenue this quarter?

Michael Chen: Sure, the 8% sequential AUM lift to $525 billion from markets, $12 billion flows, and FX directly boosted fee revenue 11% to $2.41 billion—average $512 billion at 48 bps gave $110 million organic lift, plus $85 million performance fees, offset by minimal compression through active margins.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Kline with Barclays.

Robert Kline: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of your ESG-enhanced equity strategies?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, Robert. Our ESG products outperformed, like the S&P 500 ESG Enhanced ETF at $12 billion AUM with top-quartile returns, capturing $15 billion Schwab RIA flows and €5 billion Europe, delivering 250 bps alpha via quant overlays amid SFDR/TCFD tailwinds and sustainable $40 trillion trend.

Robert Kline: And how is the new direct indexing product performing relative to expectations?

David Wong: Great question. The Wealthfront white-label exceeded with $4.2 billion HNW inflows, 20-30 bps tax-alpha, 85% six-month retention, and scaling via fractional shares—early wins validating personalization, with APIs boosting 40% adoption like Fidelity models.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Johnathan Reed for closing remarks.

Johnathan Reed: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
